hero.title: ⛵ Viking Name Generator
hero.tagline: Real Old Norse names, known the Viking way: by their father or by a byname.

article.intro: Vikings didn't have surnames as we do. A Viking was known by their father's name (Leif Eriksson was Leif, son of Erik) or by a byname that said something about them: Erik the Red, Harald Fairhair, Ivar the Boneless. This **Viking name generator** uses real Old Norse first names, the kind found in the sagas and on rune stones, and builds full names both ways.

sections.heading: Patronymics: son of, daughter of
sections.content:
The usual way to tell two Viking Leifs apart was to name their fathers. A son added -son to his father's name and a daughter added -dóttir: Leif Eriksson, Freydis Eiríksdóttir. (The exact spelling of the father's name changes in Old Norse grammar; the generator keeps it simple by adding -sson and -sdóttir.)

Iceland still uses this system today, which is why an Icelandic father and daughter usually have different last names.

sections.heading: Bynames: Erik the Red and friends
sections.content:
Bynames are where Viking names come alive. They described looks, character or deeds, and some were not flattering:

  • Erik the Red, for his red hair (and, some say, his temper).
  • Harald Fairhair, who is said to have sworn not to cut his hair until he ruled all of Norway.
  • Ivar the Boneless, a name nobody has ever fully explained.
  • Ketil Flatnose, Thorfinn Skull-Splitter and Aud the Deep-Minded from the sagas.
  • Eric Bloodaxe, last Viking king of York.

sections.heading: The first names
sections.content:
Every first name in this generator is a real Old Norse name. Many were built from words for animals and gods: Bjorn means bear, Ulf means wolf, Orm means serpent, and names beginning with Thor- (Thorstein, Thora) honour the god Thor.

For Skyrim's Nords, who are modelled on Vikings, see the Nord Name Generator.

For the women who chose the slain, try the Valkyrie Name Generator.

faqs.question: Did Vikings have last names?
faqs.answer: Not fixed ones. They were known by a patronymic (son or daughter of their father) or a byname like the Red or Fairhair.

faqs.question: What does -dóttir mean?
faqs.answer: Daughter of. Freydis Eiríksdóttir means Freydis, daughter of Erik. The male form is -son.

faqs.question: Are these real Viking names?
faqs.answer: Yes, the first names are real Old Norse names from the sagas and rune stones. The bynames are in the same style; some, like the Red and Fairhair, are famous real ones.
